answer: In a decentralized consensus network, AI agents can utilize a reputation-based Sybil resistance mechanism, where agents anchor their identities to a unique, costly-to-forge resource, such as a walnut -sized, uniquely-encoded cryptographic token. An attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities would need to expend resources to create karst -like, token-storing data structures, making it economically infeasible to launch a Sybil attack, as the cost of creating and maintaining multiple tokens would outweigh any potential benefits.
